headline: New attack on Strait of Hormuz shipping fuels fears for global oil supplies
summary: A projectile reportedly hit a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, intensifying concerns over Middle East conflicts disrupting vital oil routes. This follows a drone attack on a Saudi pipeline and Houthi advances.
details: Maritime trackers reported a new attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday. The British navy-affiliated agency UKMTO stated a projectile hit a vessel, though the extent of damage and crew status remain unknown.

This incident adds to growing concerns about threats to energy supplies, coming a day after Saudi Arabia temporarily closed its East-West pipeline. The closure was a precaution following a drone attack that both Baghdad and Riyadh attributed to Iraq, where Iranian-backed militias operate.
The escalating conflict in the Middle East could drive energy prices even higher. This past week already saw the cost of Brent crude surge back above $100 a barrel amidst rising tensions.

The 1,200-km East-West pipeline, running across the Arabian Peninsula, has been a crucial alternative route for global Middle East oil supplies for the past six months, especially as the Strait of Hormuz has faced disruptions.

This pipeline typically transports 4 million to 5 million barrels per day, accounting for 4% to 5% of global supply. This has helped shield Saudi Arabia from the severe disruptions impacting other Gulf oil and gas exporters.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the pipeline strikes. Satellite images showed black smoke rising from an area south of Medina, and the Saudi Foreign Ministry reported some injuries and damage, which is currently being assessed.

US President Donald Trump suggested Iran was likely responsible for the attacks. Separately, Saudi Civil Defence reported that a projectile fired by Houthis injured two people and damaged buildings, including a mosque, in the Jazan region.

Oil prices have surged over the past week as the US and Iran reportedly fired on tankers, and Iran-aligned Houthis advanced along the Red Sea. This Houthi movement, including the seizure of Perim island in the Bab el-Mandeb strait, risks extending disruptions to another major oil route.

Washington now faces a dilemma regarding intervention to assist the Saudis against the Houthis, which could further broaden the conflict. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman reportedly asked Trump for US military help, receiving assurances of intelligence support but no direct intervention for now.

Amidst these developments, Iran's Foreign Ministry announced it would attend a meeting with Gulf Arab states in Oman on Monday to discuss the future of the Strait of Hormuz. However, a senior Iranian official downplayed the chances of a breakthrough.

Iran seeks recognition of its control over the Strait of Hormuz, allowing it to collect fees from passing ships, a demand rejected by Washington. Oman, controlling the opposite bank, is reportedly negotiating with other regional states' agreement.

headline: Dockyard and Engineering Works Ltd. has 86 job vacancies across 35 categories
summary: Dockyard and Engineering Works (DEW) Limited, operated by the Bangladesh Navy, is recruiting 86 personnel across 35 categories of positions. The application deadline is September 19, 2026.
details: Dockyard and Engineering Works (DEW) Limited, operated by the Bangladesh Navy, has announced a recruitment drive for 86 personnel. These vacancies span 35 different categories of positions.

Among the advertised positions are Assistant Engineer (Naval Architect), LDC (Low-Grade Clerk cum Computer Operator) for P&D, HR, and Chief Store sections, and Security Guard for the Safety and Security section. This offers a wide range of opportunities for various skill sets.

For contractual appointments, selected candidates will receive basic salary along with other allowances and bonuses. Daily wage-based appointments will include daily wages/salaries and bonuses (where applicable) according to DEW Ltd.'s own pay structure, recruitment policy, Bangladesh Labor Law, and prevailing regulations.

Interested candidates must send their application forms along with necessary documents to the Managing Director, Dockyard and Engineering Works Ltd., Bangladesh Navy, Sonakanda, Bandar-1410, Bandar, Narayanganj. The final date for application submission is September 19, 2026.
